tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This statement is actually incorrect. Metolazone and hydrochlorothiazide block the sodium reabsorption at the distal convoluted tubule. Remember although we call it “tubular reabsorption and tubular secretion” the terms pertain to the peritubular capillaries. So ‘tubular reabsorption of sodium’ actually means that the sodium is being saved into the peritubular capillaries. As metolazone and hydrochlorothiazide block the tubular reabsorption, more sodium is in the tubules, pulling water into the nephron and excreting it.
